# Pandamonium v1.0.62

This patch train ships two reviewed changes: the plugin intake repair — pasting a public repository into **Add Plugins → Add from GitHub** and installing no longer requires the repository to carry a JOS-specific manifest, and the reviewed static scan draft becomes the install manifest when the pinned revision has no committed `jarvis-extension.json` while marketplace and repository manifests keep precedence — plus the Agent Identities settings slice, which turns the single installation identity into a per-session multi-identity registry with attached model profiles and a dedicated Settings tab. CT103 updates through the signed updater with rollback to v1.0.61.

## MAD-929 — Settings: Agent Identities tab with multiple saved identities and attached model profiles

### Problem

Settings could only hold a single installation identity, so the operator could not create more than one agent identity (for example Jarvis and Friday) or give each its own model profile; identity was an installation-wide setting rather than a per-session choice.

### Implementation

Commits `3a88ac7a` through `f97d2103` (PR #212, merge `3214a1c2`): a multi-identity registry (`data/agent_identities.json`) with create, edit, duplicate, and delete; a new Settings → Agent Identities tab that lists saved identities and migrates the existing installation identity as the first entry; each identity carries a constitution and an attached model profile (chat model and reasoning level with optional per-lane overrides defaulting to the chat profile); a chat session can bind one identity (`sessions.identity_id`) so its model/endpoint and reasoning level load with that session; and the first-run wizard's identity step now routes to the dedicated tab. `agent_identity_status()` and constitution validation remain the public contract, and a clean install still materializes only the generic public defaults.

### Product value and UI visibility

Settings → Agent Identities lists identities with the existing identity status badge and a per-session binding control; admins can create, edit, duplicate, and delete identities and set the attached model profile, while non-admins see the list and binding without editor controls. Reloading a session restores its bound identity's model and reasoning level, and other sessions keep the installation identity.

### Verification

256 focused Python tests passed (store CRUD, settings migration, prompt selection, route admin gating with constitution redaction, session migration columns, session binding helpers, protocol UI parity); the new `mad-929-agent-identities.spec.js` browser spec and `protocol-settings-removed.spec.js` passed; PR #212 checks green; the v1.0.62 release candidate ran the full Python and Chromium suites green on PR #215. Operator acceptance (create two identities, bind one to a chat session, reload, confirm the model and reasoning level load) remains the live check after CT103 updates.

### Configuration, compatibility, and limitations

Additive, idempotent migration (`sessions.identity_id`, `sessions.reasoning_level`); no new dependencies; voice identity and voice mapping are unchanged. MAD-906 (derive agent voice rows from configured identities) remains the tracked follow-up.

## MAD-945 — Extensions: install the reviewed scan draft when a repository has no committed jarvis-extension.json

### Problem

Add Plugins → Add from GitHub → Install plugin… always failed with `extension_manifest_missing` for arbitrary public repositories (reported with `obra/superpowers`, a 14-skill bundle). The staged scan correctly classified the repository and produced a validated draft manifest, but the lifecycle manager required the repository's own committed `jarvis-extension.json`, which no third-party repository will ever have. Skill-bundle drafts were also adapter-invalid, so even a generated draft could not install.

### Implementation

Commit `7bb3ad0b` (PR #210, merge `5eedf661`): `POST /api/extensions/plans/source` accepts the completed scan's `scan_id`; the server loads and re-validates the stored scan artifact (never a client-supplied manifest) and binds the requested source URL and resolved revision to it. `preview_source` uses the reviewed draft only when the pinned checkout has no committed manifest and no signed `expected_manifest`, recording `manifest_origin: scan_draft` plus the scan id and revision in the plan. `execute_plan` materializes the approved draft as `jarvis-extension.json` inside the installed revision and re-verifies it against the approved plan, so disable, enable, rollback, and uninstall keep working. The scanner now emits only installable skill layouts: descriptor repositories (`.codex-plugin/plugin.json` / `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`) use `codex_plugin` and include only importable skills, excluded skills are surfaced as a `skill_asset` finding, single-skill layouts use `agent_skill` with the real SKILL.md entrypoint, and unsupported multi-skill layouts produce no draft instead of a broken one. The Add Plugins UI sends the `scan_id`, labels generated drafts in the approval preview, and maps the new fail-closed codes to human next-step copy.

### Product value and UI visibility

The paste-a-link intake now matches its promise: scanning `obra/superpowers` and approving once installs 11 of its 14 skills; `brainstorming`, `subagent-driven-development`, and `writing-skills` are excluded with a visible low-severity `skill_asset` finding because their assets are `.cjs`, extensionless scripts, or `.dot`. Draft installs show a "generated draft manifest" label in the approval preview, and failures read as actionable sentences instead of raw backend codes.

### Verification

Focused Python 62 passed (scanner draft layouts, draft-install end-to-end including disable/enable/uninstall, revision/binding/draft-plus-expected-manifest negative cases, committed-manifest precedence); browser `marketplace-intake.spec.js` 4 passed; full Python 6073 passed / 5 skipped with one pre-existing order-dependent voice flake that also fails on the v1.0.61 base; full Chromium 145 passed with two pre-existing failures (`mad-846-external-agents`, `updater` worker marker) that reproduce identically on the base. Independent real-repository check against `https://github.com/obra/superpowers` at revision `b36e0829`: draft `codex_plugin`, 11 admitted skills, execute succeeded, lifecycle disable/enable/uninstall clean. PR #210 all 17 required checks green.

### Configuration, compatibility, and limitations

No dependency, database, or configuration change. The scan contract gains the additive `skill_asset` finding category (schema and validator). Marketplace signed manifests and committed repository manifests retain precedence, so existing installations are unaffected. Rollback is the previous signed release plus the updater snapshot. Limitation: skills whose bundle contains non-importable assets (`.cjs`, `.dot`, extensionless scripts) are excluded from draft installs until the skill importer's text allowlist is extended, which is a separate decision.
